utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We are now in open session. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The -- there is no dispute in this case that in the town of Bosanski Samac was a Territorial Defence office or a TO and that it was located opposite the SUP police station. In the days prior to the events of the night of the 16th and 17th of April, did you go to the TO office or at least near it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did, on the 16th of April, around 3.00, just outside the TO headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you please explain to the Chamber why you went there and what you expected to see and generally the circumstances or reasons for your attending there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw many of my fellow citizens carrying rifles, so I went there too. When I arrived outside the TO headquarters, I saw weapons were being distributed and I saw this Marko Blazanovic, Alija Fitozovic, Vlado Jasenica distributing arms, and I think Milos Bogdanovic was there on behalf of the TO headquarters. I looked up at the upper floor and I saw the Serbian police watching. I didn't dare take a rifle, and I went back home empty-handed. I thought there was some murky business involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I want to know is precisely why you went there. You've already said that you saw many of your fellow citizens carrying rifles. So you went there too. Is that the only reason?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Please carry on and answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. Some kind of doubt crept into me. I saw many people carrying weapons and I thought why shouldn't I have one too? And that's the reason why I -- why I went there. I started disbelieving my own convictions as to what was going to happen the next day. As I said, I was overcome by doubt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how many men were gathered receiving arms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my estimate, around 30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of weapons were being distributed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think those Kalashnikov automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you remain at the scene observing what was going on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ten minutes each time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean each time? Did you go more than once?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only once.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter's correction, the witness said, "Well, ten minutes," not "ten minutes each time." MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And approximately how long before the events of the 16th and 17th of April did this occasion occur when you went to the TO and saw the distribution of weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went on the 17th, in the afternoon, outside the TO, and that's when they were distributing weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry Your Honours the witness said 16th and in the transcript it said 17th if that can be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The last answer. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, I noticed that and I'm grateful to my learned friend for pointing that mistake out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the transcript says that you went to the TO, to watch the distribution of these weapons, on the 17th of April -- or the 17th, and I assume you meant the 17th of April. Is that what you meant to say or did you in fact say or did you give us a different date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I couldn't have gone on the 17th. It's a mistake. I went there on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any views or expectations as to whether or not you would be accepted into any sort of Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I wasn't either hoping or wishing that I would get one --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've described what you actually saw, namely the distribution of weapons to the men who were assembled at the TO. Did you have any knowledge or information as to who had organised this, who was distributing these weapons, whether it was indeed something to do with the TO or something else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was the job of the Territorial Defence because I saw people around who had worked in the Territorial Defence before, Dzemal Kapetanovic, Sarahudin Nogic, Milos Bogdanovic and other people who had worked in the Territorial Defence before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you assist the Court in commenting on the ethnic background of the men who were assembled at the TO receiving the weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the police officers who were observing what was going on from across the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry there is no answer recorded in our transcript. The question, is to be absolutely clear, what sort of ethnic background were the police officers who you have said were observing events from the SUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone ask you if you were in possession of a weapon at any time on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, my brother [redacted] asked me, not on the 17th but on the night of the 17th, that's when he asked me, but during the day of the 17th, nobody asked me if I had any weapons or if I wished to have a weapon. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Perhaps if we deal with Mr. Zecevic's concern first and then we can deal with mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is again the same situation, Your Honours. The witness was talking about the night of the 16th, between the 16th and the 17th and in the transcript it says the 17th so if it can be clarified? MR. DI FAZIO: I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Perhaps in Serbo-Croat the numbers 16 and 17 are very similar. MR. DI FAZIO: That might be the explanation. I don't think there is any doubt in the witness's mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: This is the second time. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can't explain it, Witness, but it seems you said the 17th of April, is that the date that you said or meant, or did you have in mind another date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 16th. I meant the 16th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And I want to ask you now about what your brother said but don't use his name at the moment because it's a matter that tends to identify you. We know which brother you're talking about. Can you tell us what -- the circumstances of his questioning you about a weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He thought that I had taken the weapon. He told me if I had Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. one, that I should hand it over to him and then I would have no problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did he say this to you and about what time did he say this to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said that on the 16th of April, in the evening, sometime around 6.00 p.m. in my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he give you a reason for his asking you this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He did say that the army would enter Samac, that I should not open the doors to anyone, and that I should sit tight at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- what did you say to him when he asked you to hand over any weapon that you might have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told him I had no weapons, which was indeed the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the middle of the night were you awoken by the sound of gunfire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you remain at home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you about the morning, following the gunfire that you heard. That is the morning of the 17th of April, 1992. That morning, did you see any soldiers, paramilitary types?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they amongst those people, were there any locals that you knew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were some local Serbs from Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were their names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fadil Topcagic, Jovo Ikamovic, Milan Celikovic and Drago Borovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've described them as local Serbs. Does Fadil Topcagic come into that category?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, since he changed his name, I do consider him to be a local Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can you tell the Chamber how they were dressed when you first saw them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were dressed in camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice anything about their faces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I did notice some new insignia they had, the new Serbian army insignia, the tricolour on their hats and on their right shoulder, they had some multi-coloured rags. Their faces were painted with some kind of paint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any armoured vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see them when you first laid eyes on them and under what circumstances did you see them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw them in front of my house with a Praga gun and they were shouting, "Surrender your weapons." I went out. I saw them there, they called me over the loudspeaker, the bullhorn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the call to surrender your weapon a call directed, as far as you could tell, to you personally or was it a call that was being directed to the townspeople?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was directed to me personally because they were standing outside of my window, the window on my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The armoured vehicle, did it have a small cannon or a machine-gun on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a Praga gun with -- it had three barrels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were those barrels trained or directed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right at my windows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having been told to surrender your weapon and faced with this Praga with its guns pointing at your home, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went out and stood in front of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have your hands up or did you do anything to show surrender?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had my hands up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having obviously surrendered with your hands up, what did the group of men do?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He told me to go back in my house. And I ran into my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I fully understand how difficult it is, but if you could just try and remember not to refer to your brothers by name at this stage. Just refer to your brothers if it comes up again, okay? Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, with all due respect, regarding this specific situation, but we know that this witness has several brothers and for the purposes of this transcript, and for the -- this particular proceedings, it might be to some extent maybe tomorrow difficult to clarify all these details, so I would suggest if we are going to discuss all these matters, to go into private session or just for a while. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: I fully take Mr. Pantelic's point. I think it's well made but I don't think it's going to arise as a particular issue at this stage. There will be reference to the brothers at a later point of time. We can go into private session then so that we are clearly identifying which brother is which so the Defence won't be left in any doubt as to who the witness is talking about. I'll ensure that that's covered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So for the time being we remain in open session. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did Fadil Topcagic hit you so that you fell to the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He kicked me with his boots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the men remain at your home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They never entered my house. I came out of my house. And this is where it all happened, in front of my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But what I mean is how long did all the events just outside your house take? How long did the whole episode take?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ten to 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you injured as a result of being kicked on the ground and the attack on you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had some injuries on my ribs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did these soldiers apparently accept your explanation that you had no weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they say or do anything that indicated they didn't believe you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the Serb told Fadil whose brother I was, then Fadil let me go, although Fadil knows my brother very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The next topic I want to ask you about is events at a place called Buducnost or the Buducnost factory. Do you know of such a factory in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go there at all after the 17th of April? Just answer me yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under what circumstances did you find yourself to be going to the Buducnost factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All men of military age and all men able to work were summoned to the Buducnost factory to report there. I think it was the Sunday, the 20th. That was when we had to report there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you become aware of this obligation to report at the Buducnost factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because there were posters put up in Bosanski Samac and also the police went around in a Zastava 128 police car with a loudspeaker informing people about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doing the best you can, what was the precise message that was being conveyed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That we should report, all the men of military age, to the Buducnost factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Did you -- I think you went along on the Sunday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you dress in any particular way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I was not dressed in any particular way. I just had to wrap a white rag around my right arm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you wrap a white rag around your right arm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So that they could tell the non-Serb population of Samac from the rest. That was some kind of a permit for you. You could dare -- you could then walk around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you find out about the -- that particular device, separating you from Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That morning, I met a friend of mine who was out for a walk, Djoko Pisarevic. I asked him, "Can I go out?" And he told me, "Just wrap a white rag around your left arm." And that's how I learned about that, from him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you eventually make it to the Buducnost factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone else have white rags wrapped around their arm or any sort of white emblem on their arms or shoulders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We all had them, all of us gathered there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many men were gathered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between 200 and 300.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the way to the factory, what sort of conditions were prevailing in Bosanski Samac? And by that, I mean any signs of destruction or damage to property, and soldiers or military vehicles on the street. What did you notice or see in respect of those two matters, if anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I noticed that the licence plates on all the vehicles that said the Army of Republika Srpska, and I asked myself, "When in God's name did they manage to make all those licence plates? They only had three days to do that, yet they somehow managed to do it."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when you got to the Buducnost factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jovo Savic spoke to us, addressed us then. He told us to take our weapons and defend our town against the Ustashas. An incident occurred then. They were asking for Igor Rukavina. I saw him personally but I did not report him. After a while, Igor himself said that he was present. A military truck came. They put Igor on the truck and started kicking him. Then I noticed an unknown officer of the Serbian army, who said that the rally was over, the meeting was over, and that if anyone had any questions, they could ask them -- they could talk to General Adzic and that is how this meeting, this gathering, ended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Firstly, were you left -- I'll withdraw that question. Did you receive or did you receive or did anyone get any explanation as to why Rukavina was being arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they told us that he was a sniper, a sniper shooter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the meeting conclude with any firm or clear instructions as to what you were to do in order to defend yourself against the Ustasha or any other instructions at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They told us to take our weapons but since the gathering ended rather abruptly, we did not receive any clear instructions as to what we were to do tomorrow, the next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The men who arrested Mr. Rukavina, were any of them local men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognised Miki Jovicic; he drove the truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Miki Jovicic a member of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Following the meeting, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went back to our homes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you walk home with anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went with Namik Vajzovic and Hris Hadzikadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of an establishment called Cafe AS in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your path home take you close or near to Cafe AS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, right past this cafe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anything happen to you as you walked past or got close to the Cafe AS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Court what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I came to the Cafe AS, Mr. Corolic called me by my nickname. I turned around. I looked, and two armed Serb soldiers jumped and dragged me to the Cafe AS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I just interrupt you there? First of all, can I ask you who is Mr. Corolic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He owned a catering business in Samac. He was also a member of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of what ethnic background is he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was he when he called you by your nickname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was sitting in the garden of the Cafe AS, the open-air part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, these -- he called out your nickname and you were then grabbed or assaulted by two armed Serb soldiers. I want you to continue on from there but also, can you first tell us if the Serb soldiers were locals or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of them was a local and one of them was from Serbia. He was a special, a member of the Special Forces. When I sat down, they started beating me. One of them was called Nebosja Stankovic and the other was nicknamed Sumadinac

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Nebosja Stankovic, did he have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Cera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did they beat you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With a pistol. He hit me with a pistol, on the clavicles, on my head, then he stuck a knife into my right arm to see whether the balija blood was green. After a long beating, I fainted. When I came to, I was all wet because somebody had thrown water over me and I heard somebody laughing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the beating take place? Was it inside the cafe or just outside in the garden?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the garden.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where on your arm were you stabbed with the knife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On my right arm, into the muscle here, on the upper arm. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, the witness indicates his right, upper, inner arm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that you were -- you lost consciousness and that you eventually woke and that you had had water thrown over you and that you heard laughter. When you came to, did you notice any people about you or standing about you, or in the very near vicinity, and if so, were you able to identify them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw Mr. Miroslav Tadic standing there in the doorway at the entrance to the cafe. There was Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you heard laughter upon your regaining consciousness. Can you attribute that laughter to anyone or is it the case that you just don't know who it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just heard laughter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened once you had regained consciousness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They ordered me to stand up. They got into a white Kadett car, and I had to run all the way to the Samac SUP with my hands up, shouting, "Serbia, Serbia."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just before we get to that part of your ordeal, I'd like to ask you this: You were ordered to stand up and presumably ordered to get into a car. Who was giving these orders to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not get into the car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. My apologies. I apologise for that. You were ordered to get in front of the car and run. But what I'm concerned about is this: Who gave you these orders, who instructed you to get up and run in front of the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That member of the Special Forces, by the name of Sumadinac. He ordered me to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in the period of time just before you were beaten in the Cafe AS, you saw 4th Detachment soldiers, a 4th Detachment soldier, in the garden, Serbian soldiers in the garden, after you regained consciousness, the Serbian soldiers were there, plus Mr. Tadic and Mr. Simo Zaric. Is that a correct assessment of the personalities present before and after your beating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you had to run in front of the car shouting, "Serbia, Serbia." How far did you have to run engaged in this sort of behaviour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around a kilometre and a half. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to do it? Or did you fall down or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I managed to do it but barely. I couldn't keep my hands up because both my clavicles were broken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far behind you was the car travelling when you were running on the way to the SUP shouting, "Serbia, Serbia"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 20 metres behind me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you hear anything coming from the car, any sound?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very simple sounds, shouting, shrieking laughter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the car itself, do you know who owned the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, tell us who was the owner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Safet Dagovic from Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What ethnic background is he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened once you had arrived at the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then Mirko Pavic was on duty at the time. The policeman. He told those two to leave me alone and went upstairs to check my papers to see if I was on any of the lists. Since I was not, he ordered eight policemen to go with me to check my apartment, and that's what they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you went back to your home with these policemen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they search the premises?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they arrest you or did they eventually leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did not arrest me. They even dragged me to the health centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you eventually treated at the health centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What injuries did -- or rather what injuries were you informed you had suffered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two clavicles fractured as well as two fingers on my right hand, and knife cut on my right arm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you hospitalised at all or were you treated and allowed to go home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was just bandaged and allowed to go home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you -- how long were you recovering from these injuries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 15 to 20 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that time, did you report anywhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had to report every morning to the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you, in fact, carry out that reporting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours would just bear with me for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. [Prosecution counsel confer]. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a minor matter, Witness. Earlier you described the car that followed you as you were calling out, "Serbia, Serbia," and so on. Were the two men who were inside the car -- who were they, first of all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nebosja Stankovic, nicknamed Cera, and this Sumadinac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anyone else or was that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just the two of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the reporting to the SUP, did anyone ever explain to you why you should report on a daily basis to the SUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the occasions that you went to the SUP for this reporting business while you were recovering from your injuries, did you ever see any of the defendants at the SUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Over what period of time did you report to the SUP? I'm not necessarily asking for dates, although if you can give us dates, please do. But was it a couple of weeks that you were reporting to the SUP, or was it a month? Just give us as much information about dates and period of time that you were reporting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around three weeks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that would have taken you into May that you were reporting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many times did you see Mr. Zaric at the SUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see a lot of him, but I did see him three or four times in the time while I was reporting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember what he was doing, how he was dressed, under what circumstances you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what he was doing there, but he was wearing a military uniform, complete with a pistol, of course, and when I was going into or coming out of the SUP building, of course, we met.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever speak to him? Or did he ever speak to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was said and by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I didn't know how to be a gentleman, then I should be a slave. That's what he said to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how this comment was prompted, if indeed it was prompted by anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you reply?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't. I didn't dare to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long had you known Mr. Simo Zaric at the time that the comment was made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you mean before the war?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For a long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever socialised with him or had any sort of dealings with him, either on a professional or work or social basis or was it just that you knew him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just knew him. We were acquaintances and in his home village of Tursinovac we sometimes sat down after a game, but it was rather superficial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew him as a doctor, but ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you known him and under what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For a while, he was my teacher in the secondary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Milan Simic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you known him -- or had you known him at -- as at April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see him at all in the April of 1992, and I had known him for a long time because he was a neighbour and he lived just across my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look around the Court, can you, and if you can see any of the men that I've asked you about, can you please point them out to the Chamber and identify them? Identify them one by one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first in the row, Dr. Blagoje Simic in the first row. In the back row, Mr. Miroslav Tadic, Mr. Simo Zaric and Mr. Milan Simic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If Your Honours please, may the record reflect that the witness correctly identified the defendants?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, eventually you must have recovered from your injuries or recovered to a degree from your injuries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you start working at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like you now to tell us about that and can you inform the Chamber first of all how -- the circumstances under which you came to be informed of the need to work and about when this was made known to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was sometime in the second half of the month of May. I don't know whether it was the 16th or the 17th. A messenger came to see me, Mr. Kosta Radic. He brought a piece of paper for me to sign and told me to report the next day outside the SDK building in order to be sent to that labour brigade, as they called it, to do my work duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the SDK building? Does it house any particular type of institution or does it carry out a certain function?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are two institutions in that building. The downstairs was occupied by the government auditing agency and upstairs there was the communications centre which belonged to the headquarters of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the piece of paper that you were given by Kosta Radic spell out that you were to be sent to a labour brigade or was that something that you found out afterwards? In other words, I'm concerned to know what precisely the piece of paper told you was going to happen, even before you got to the SDK building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were several names on that piece of paper, including mine, and I was to sign that piece of paper and report the next morning at 7.00 a.m. at the SDK building. I didn't know what to expect and what would happen there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Did you in fact report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the Chamber what you saw when you reported the next morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw about 100 of my fellow citizens, townsfolk who were waiting outside the building. Nobody knew what they were waiting for, where they were going or what was going to happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this point of time, had you recovered from your broken -- from the injuries to your clavicles, your broken clavicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What ethnic background were the assembled people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you assemble outside the SDK building or inside it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Outside the building. We didn't enter. We were just outside the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'd like to know is this: Before you got to the SDK building and found yourself standing there just outside it, did you have any idea what was going to be said to you or did you have any idea as to what the reason was for your assembling there or is it the case that you only found out once you arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I learned about that only when I had come already outside the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell the Chamber how you learned about what the purpose was in your going there and what happened once you arrived.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we arrived, the lists were read out to us. In fact, they called out our names to see if everyone had responded to the call-up. Since most people had, they went upstairs into the building. I think it was Dzemal Kapetanovic and the other one was Bozo Ninkovic. After a while we were divided into those labour groups. We didn't know where we were going or what we were required to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you -- when you say people went upstairs into the building, was that the assembled crowd, or is it -- or are you referring to Dzemal Kapetanovic and Bozo Ninkovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I mean Dzemal and Bozo Ninkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any armed soldiers or guards about the place at the time of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were divided into groups and where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On to trucks. The trucks were parked there. We -- they put us on to trucks and took us to our work sites.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know where you were going when you were placed on to a truck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there guards -- or rather armed guards on the truck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many people were on your truck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean the people who were working?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Unless I misunderstood your evidence, you were separated into groups, including you. You were placed on a truck and then taken off to your work site. What I want to know is how many people were on your particular truck, what sort of groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 15 to 20 men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took us to various locations. We never had a permanent work site or anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall where your very first assignment was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was digging trenches at Zasavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you remain on that particular project?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were shifted around very often but we would spend sometimes two or three days in one location, depending on the work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I understand that to mean that you worked at Zasavica for a period of a few days and then might work somewhere else and then were taken back to Zasavica? Is that a correct understanding or did you do your work at Zasavica in one block, to so speak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, just amplify that a bit and explain to us how the projects were divided up time-wise. Did you work at Zasavica for a long time and then were taken somewhere else or what? Explain it a bit more carefully, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We would get our work assignment, for instance digging trenches. When we finished that job, we moved to another place. It all depended on the length of the trenches, but we would spend two, three, four, maybe five days on one location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you about Zasavica. Were there soldiers there where you were digging the trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there gunfire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once, when three of my fellow citizens had escaped across the Bosna, they opened fire after them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just tell the Chamber what exactly digging trenches at Zasavica involved.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We dug trenches at Zasavica in front of the combat lines in order to come as close to the Bosna River as possible. We were not safe. There was shooting and all they had to say was, "Those are your own people. They won't shoot at you." Nevertheless, a couple of my fellow citizens did get killed while digging.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that at Zasavica or was that elsewhere digging trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Zasavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you there at the time or is this something that you heard about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When Dzevad Murkic got killed, I wasn't there that day. I wasn't around. I was a little further on. And when Idrizi Redzep got killed, I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Idrizi killed at Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that during your first assignment there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not really. It was a little later, about eight days after I started working, towards the end of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Witness, if you could look at P9. Get him to look at P9 and just draw where the front line is along Zasavica. MR. DI FAZIO: I'll do that, if Your Honours please. If Your Honours please, I've got a clean copy of P9 which we can introduce into evidence but for -- yes, I have a completely clean copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So we can have it given a number. MR. DI FAZIO: Mr. Usher, might I ask you, please, to present this to the witness. I see no reason why it shouldn't be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, can we maybe just check for a second this map in order to verify this is actually P9 exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I'd just like to clarify that in indeed P9 is the map of Zasavica -- of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which includes -- MR. DI FAZIO: Which includes that town. I just want to make sure there is no mistake about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, my learned colleague. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It can be placed on the ELMO. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Witness, have a look at the map there. Find Zasavica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you found it? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, looking at that map, could you please mark on that map in pen -- and I perhaps -- with that green marking pen that the usher has -- could you indicate a line where the trenches were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right. [Marks] . Here were the trenches that were dug in the direction of the Bosna River. And the trenches went this way. It was about 100 metres from the Bosna River an those were access roads to the Bosna River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I ask you to just mark a little more clearly, if you can, in firmer, clearer lines, the trenches, the trench system? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Witness. MR. DI FAZIO: Can that be produced into evidence, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, can we have the number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit P9-I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And are what are you going to call it? MR. DI FAZIO: We can entitle it, "Map drawn by Witness M indicating trench layout at Zasavica".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Marked in green. MR. DI FAZIO: Marked in green, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd just like to ask you one or two more questions while the map is still on the ELMO. Looking at the map, Witness, you've indicated that the trench line ran somehow almost parallel or close to the river, which I think is the Bosna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there were also trenches going in towards the river, access trenches, so to speak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the purpose of the access trenches? If that's indeed what they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We didn't know what we were digging but later events taught us, because those trenches were needed for the attack on Odzak and the entire Odzak municipality, for the forced crossing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the access trenches, did they come down towards the water line or close to the river?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They came very close to the river. They stopped just two or three metres away from the Sava River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you and your fellow workers ever work on the access trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone ever try to escape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And before we break off, can we just get clarification? Is that River Bosna or Sava River? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Bosna.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. It's 11.00. We will have our break and continue at 11.30 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Prosecution is continuing with examination-in-chief. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, before the break, we were talking about the trench -- trenches that you worked on at Zasavica and -- you mentioned the access trenches and you also said that people tried to escape. From where within that trench system did people try to escape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you want me to show it or ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can probably describe it adequately in your own words. If necessary, I'll ask you to show it on the map, but you just tell us in your own words from where they tried to escape.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From -- as we dug the connecting or access trenches, three people escaped on one occasion. I cannot really pinpoint the location on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I want to know is this: Did they try -- did they make their escape bids or successful escapes from the access trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that when they were close to the water?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell the Chamber how they actually escaped.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As we dug at one of the access trenches, we reached a place which was about 2 metres away from the River Bosna so they jumped into the water and crossed to the other side. The Serbian soldiers shot at them but the side on the opposite -- the people on the opposite side returned fire and they managed to escape into the Odzak municipality using this exchange of fire as a cover.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And on how many occasions did people escape in this manner by leaping into the water and swimming across to the other side whilst digging trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While I was there, the three people managed to escape, there were some other cases but I was not present on those places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From whom did you hear of the other cases of escape? Was it from fellow workers or in some other way that you were informed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the others, but we would go back together on trucks and that's how we received our information as we sat down on the trucks, they would tell us such and such a person escaped or we would tell each other who managed to -- who had managed to escape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst you were digging the trenches, either the trenches that ran parallel to the river or the access trenches, were you exposed to gunfire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the -- sorry. I'll withdraw that question and rephrase it. When Serbian guns fired, were they in front of you as you dug on the trenches or behind you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were behind us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any way of knowing when gunfire was about to erupt when you were working on the trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no way to know that. We never knew to anticipate -- we could never anticipate when the gunfire would be opened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You also mentioned that in addition to escape attempts, some people were killed while digging trenches. Can you just tell us about the cases that you are aware of, where the people were killed and whether or not you were present or you learnt of it from others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When Redzep, Idrizi got killed, I was there. There was gunfire, an exchange of fire between the warring factions and a bullet hit him. The bullet came from across the Bosna, from the Odzak municipality. He fell. He was put on to the truck. And he died on the way to hospital. When Dzevad Murkic was killed, I was not there. A bullet was fired and it hit him while he was on the truck as they were loading the tools, shovels and so on, on to the truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was -- in the case of the latter name that you mentioned, Dzevad, was that at a trench-digging location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in Pisari. It was towards the place where the River Sava, the River Bosna joins the River Sava.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But all I want to know is this: You say that he was killed while loading, tools, shovels and so on, on to a truck. What I want to know is, if you know, can you tell us whether that was on completion of a trench-digging job or was it some other type of work? It's just the type of work that he was doing at the time that he was killed that I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was getting into the truck. The tools were already on the truck and as he was getting on to the truck, a bullet was fired and it hit him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand that. All I want to know is this: Before he was fired on, had he been working on trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when the other gentleman you mentioned, Mr. Idriz was killed, was that on the trench job at Zasavica or was it some other location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Zasavica as we were digging trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just answer me yes or no to the next question, if you can. Did you ever do labour in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About when did you start doing that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When Odzak fell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'll ask you about Odzak at a later point of time. I'm now going to concentrate on the period of time when you first started doing this labour up until the time you were transferred to Odzak, so the period of time when you were still in the main -- working in Bosanski Samac. You've described trench digging and one of the occasions was at Zasavica. Did you ever do trench digging at any other locations apart from Zasavica and before you went to Odzak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you do trench digging?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I dug trenches in the village much Grebnice and Tramosnica

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at the map, P9-I that you have on the ELMO. Can you see Tramosnica anywhere there on the map or is the map covering an area that's too small?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The village of Grebnice is not here on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I don't think that that is -- that map will show the -- is big enough to show the towns. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I was wondering whether it's really necessary for the Prosecution case to show all the trenches, where they were dug. I think it's sufficient to simply mention the place or the village and simply say trenches were dug. MR. DI FAZIO: Very well. Thank you, Your Honour. I won't pursue that matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There was particular interest in the other one perhaps because of the crossings across the river. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, thank you. All right. Thank you, Mr. Usher, I've finished with that map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you just tell us briefly, Witness, if in the villages of Grebnice and the other village that you mentioned, whether you were exposed to gunfire on the occasions that you were digging trenches there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you guarded there by armed soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, again concentrating on the period of time before you went to -- or started to go to Odzak, apart from digging trenches, did you engage in any other sort of labour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Looting of Croat homes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There are of course villages surrounding Bosanski Samac and I don't think it's in dispute that the villages are -- were populated by either Croats or Serbs, in the main, but that there were very -- there were no Muslim villages. Is that something that you would agree with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you looted in a village, was it easy to tell if the village was Croat or Serb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the Chamber how the looting process would start, how you went about it, how goods were gathered and taken away.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the morning, when we went to a village, we went there by truck and we would go from house to house and take stuff out into the street. Another group would come and load the things that we had taken out on to trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall when you would be told which village that you were going to? Was it something that you were informed of in the morning or would it only become clear once you arrived at your destination?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We would learn about the village, the name of the village, only when we arrived there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you receive instructions as to what to take out of the houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We received instructions from whoever was escorting us, the driver and the armed escort, the armed soldiers who were escorting us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of goods were looted from the houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The household appliances, furniture, water supply equipment, water heating facilities, TV sets, VCRs, everything that was of any value was taken out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where would it be placed once it was taken out of the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We loaded this on to trucks. In fact, it was not us but a special group that was tasked with putting this on to trucks. We would just take the goods out and put them on to the pavement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a situation where you were organised into groups that distinguished between those who would go into the homes and loot and those who would be organised into collecting the looted goods?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell the Chamber of the ethnic background of the inhabitants of the villages that -- where you looted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exclusively Croat villages were looted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And, Mr. di Fazio, the Trial Chamber would like some details as you lead your evidence because of these paragraphs in the indictment, such as paragraph E on page 5, saying "the wanton and extensive destruction, plundering and looting of the property," blah, blah, blah. So the elements of those offences, I think, the details should be extracted, if available, where the witnesses know what was going on. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. If you mean was there -- if you're interested in any evidence of wanton and extensive destruction in the villages, then that's something I can explore with the witness but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Well, it's your indictment. It's up to the way you understand it, so you extract the evidence which you think will go to prove those allegations. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I'll ask about that, but I would think that this evidence is going to concentrate very much on the looting aspect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I know, but this is just one of the witnesses. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us that the -- the plunder and the looting and the -- the organised fashion in which it was carried out and the fact that it was confined to Croatian villages. When I say that, I mean inhabited by Croats. Was there any damage committed to the villages themselves, any sort of destruction or wanton sort of damage? Or was it simply a case of carrying out of the looting in these Croatian villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Damage was inflicted. Quite a few houses were burned, and as far as I think, it was not just looting but destruction too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Was that -- who inflicted this damage that you observed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Local Serbs, the Serb troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went into these Croatian villages or -- I'm sorry, I keep saying Croatian villages but I mean villages inhabited by Croats -- were the work teams carrying out the looting the only people present, or were there soldiers about the place as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were soldiers there so that there was a race of sorts, who would be the first to grab as many things and loot as many things from the Croat villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the work groups in which you were participating have to compete with the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this happen in every village or was it only occasionally that this sort of -- that you ran into this sort of competition, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time I saw that was in the village of Hasici. It was a Croat village where the villagers of Skaric competed with us as to who would loot more houses. They used to say that they were going shopping to Hasici, that's what the Serbs from Skaric said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you list the names for the Chamber of the villages that you went to and looted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hrvatska Tisina, Gornji and Donji Hasici, Gornica, Tramosnica and a part of Grebnice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In every case that you have just mentioned, was there the same level of organisation that you have described, namely assembling in the morning, being transported in trucks, looting the houses, placing the material in the street, others tasked with the collection of the looted goods? Was that basic procedure adopted in respect of the villages that you have mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And were these activities always carried out under armed guard? MR. DI FAZIO: Sorry, that's -- thank you, Your Honour. That's one other feature that the Chamber wishes to know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were carrying out these looting activities in these villages, were there armed guards with you? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now I'm still asking you about the period of time before Odzak. You've described trenches and looting. Any other sort of activity that you carried out in -- whilst doing this labour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I also performed my work as a plumber quite a lot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. di Fazio, before you move on, I'd like to ask the witness in the Croat populated villages, where you were participating under guard in the looting, do you know what had happened to the Croat inhabitants of those villages, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do know. They all fled from those villages. The troops that were in Kornica, the Croat troops that were in Kornica, withdrew towards Modrica. The population of Hrvatska Tisina took shelter in Grebnice which was controlled by the HVO. Quite a few people from Hasici were imprisoned in the camps around Samac. Tramosnica joined Gradacac -- I mean the population went to the other side which was controlled by the BH army. So that the houses were abandoned, left empty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And the witness should also explain, if he knows, when they were looting, collecting all these appliances and furniture and things, on whose behalf were they doing this? MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You remember the other discussion the other time of the army having paramilitaries or criminals as part of the army and that was a whole argument as to who is who and whose orders was anybody doing anything. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Her Honour's question takes us, I think, back to the mornings before you went to -- went out on this looting. Who would come out and read the instructions to the assembled workers as to where they should go and so on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dzemal often addressed us, as did Bozo Ninkovic, and they would always say that we were doing this on behalf of the Republika Srpska, that this was our work duty, our work obligation, that we had to carry out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of any local body or organisation from whom the work obligation or work duty was controlled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was called the Crisis Staff of the Municipal Assembly of the municipality of Serbian Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Sorry, who is Bozo Ninkovic? What's his rank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what rank he held, but I know he accompanied us while we were doing our work duty, and wherever there was a signature, whenever there was something signed, it said Bozo Ninkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Was he police or was he from the Serb army or paramilitary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think he was a member of the Serbian army. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you think it was the Crisis Staff of the Municipal Assembly of the municipality of Serbian Samac that was the body that was controlling this. Tell the Chamber why you say that. Is it something that you heard or saw or read? Your sources of information are what interest me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we were signing our call-ups for the work obligation, these papers always said, underneath, the Crisis Staff of the Samac municipality, but I didn't know who the president of the Crisis Staff was. I never saw a signature in its entirety. MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just bear with me? There is just one matter that I want to quickly check in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you carried out your looting, did you ever see anyone, either the guard or the truck driver or anyone in your group, recording or making any record of any nature whatsoever of the stuff that was taken and from where it was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't see anyone, and we were not allowed to have any pencils, let alone write anything down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to the material once the truck had come along and collected it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was taken to enterprises Mladost and Tekstilac. That's where they drove those things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever personally go to Mladost or Tekstilac to unload trucks or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Can you just include clarification on whose trucks these were? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Her Honour wishes to know the trucks that played a role in this looting, so let's look at it from every aspect. Did they have any insignia on them? Did they use the same trucks that transported people for taking away the goods or did they use separate trucks? Can you answer -- that's a double-barrelled question, but can you answer both parts: Insignia and did they use the trucks for taking the people and the goods?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All the trucks bore the emblems of the Army of Republika Srpska, the VRS, and they often used trucks of various enterprises, such as Buducnost, Mebos and others who had plenty of trucks and sometimes they used the same trucks that had brought us. While we were inside, taking things out, they would use the truck to transport the goods away and then the truck would come back. It would make two trips.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In summary, therefore, you had army trucks, and trucks belonging to commercial type of enterprises. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from army trucks and commercial trucks of commercial enterprises, were there any what I would call strictly private vehicles, that is vehicles that belonged to individuals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where those vehicles came from, the ones that belonged to the individuals that were used in the looting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They frequently came from Pisari, Crkvina, Krusko Polje, Gornji Slatina. Those were Serbian villages. They looted whatever caught their eye, as well as cattle, cows, calves, pigs. They would load them on to trucks and take them away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Those two enterprises, Buducnost and Mladost, were they state enterprises or privately owned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm afraid your answer doesn't quite answer his Honour's question because we are not sure what you mean. Were they state enterprises or were they privately owned or were they both?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were state enterprises, Mebos and Buducnost. MR. DI FAZIO: I also don't think Your Honour's question has been properly recorded in the transcript. Perhaps the court reporters could note that and rectify that at some stage. I don't think we need to clarify this at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I think the scenario now from the witness's evidence, there appear to be some private vehicles, trucks from state enterprises and then trucks from the army. I'm concerned with organisation and control. Again with the looting and the taking away of the goods. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The trucks, the private vehicles, were there different groups or were the trucks belonging to the army and to the state enterprises under one control? If so, how did it appear to the witness who was there on the scene? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Her Honour is concerned to know whether the trucks that you have described as participating in the looting, were all part of one organisation or whether there were different people using those trucks for looting. In other words, were they privately looting or not? Now, you've told us already that the soldiers were involved in their own looting and you've told us of the role that you played and the organised fashion. But what about these other trucks that you have described, the ones used -- the ones that came from the commercial enterprises like Buducnost?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It often happened that a driver would take the truck usually drove for his enterprise and come to loot for his personal purposes, private looting, sort of. And there was no particular organisation involved. Whoever came first would grab whatever he could lay his hands on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: You were with armed guards. Did these armed guards which accompanied you try to stop them from looting these other people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've mentioned that you would assemble in the mornings, your task would be given to you and that you thought that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry the transcript doesn't show when the witness was mentioning something about the murder concerning this looting? If this can be clarified, please? The question before, the answer was: "It often happened that a driver would take the truck usually drove for the enterprise and come to loot for his personal purposes." And then the witness says, "That even involved the murder."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Counsel, can you clarify that with the witness? MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the murder that you referred to in an earlier answer? What was that about? Under what circumstances did it occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Marko Evdzinic from Krusko Polje came, for instance, to the Hasici village and started dismantling the boiler from the bathroom and then a Serb refugee from Srnice told him, "Don't touch that. I am occupying this house now." There ensued an argument and that Serb killed Marko Evdzinic right there in the bathroom

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What ethnic background was Marko Evdzinic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it the case that this was a brawl over looted goods?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, just getting back to the issue of organisation, please. You've told us that the -- you gathered in the mornings and tasks were given to you, that you were given. Did the same pattern apply with armed guards, and that you -- the same pattern applied in the sense of target of -- namely Croat villages. You also said and gave your reasons as to why you thought that the Crisis Staff was organised -- was connected with the organisation of that. You then went on to describe trucks that were used.
