When you were carrying out that sort of organised looting that you have described, were trucks used from private, commercial enterprises such as Buducnost and the other enterprise that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Buducnost and Mebos are not privately owned enterprises but their trucks, together with the drivers, had been requisitioned so the same drivers continued to drive those trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I want to know is those trucks --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The translation is not accurate. It is not requisitioned. It is -- he has been not been requisitioned -- they were mobilised. He said, they were mobilised, not requisitioned. The witness said the drivers and the trucks were mobilised, in B/C/S language. Is that correct, Witness? So he confirmed. It was not requisitioned. It's another word. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe while we are at it, Mr. di Fazio, you may as well get into the details so that we understand the difference between requisitioning and mobilising. MR. DI FAZIO: I'll do that if, Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And also commandeering. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you got any idea as to how these trucks from these enterprises came to be used in the process of looting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no control over that of any kind, and often this Marko Evdzinic whom I mentioned before, he was a driver for the Buducnost enterprise. In fact, no, I'm mistaken. It was his brother Skaja, whereas Marko was a mason. And Skaja would often take a truck and come around. He needed this or that. There was no control over who was taking what. And where they were driving it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how the drivers who drove the trucks that took you to the looting locations were selected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think they had received those military call-ups because all of them were Serbs. They were wearing uniforms and they could move around those villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to be absolutely clear on these -- on the use of the enterprise trucks. Were you taken to the looting locations in such trucks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've also mentioned military-type trucks. Were you taken to the looting locations in such trucks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not in military trucks. We were not driven in military trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking back, thinking back now, of the trucks that took you to the looting locations, the villages where the looting occurred, were they mainly trucks belonging to these private enterprises or were they mainly trucks belonging to private individuals, or were they a combination of both?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were many trucks that belonged to those enterprises, as well as private vehicles such as trucks, tractors and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you assembled in the mornings to be given your assignment, were the trucks already there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the drivers and the guards already there assembled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From -- I'll withdraw that. Someone gave the instructions in the morning. From where did that person emerge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the communications centre. She would climb down and get out into the yard and then they would -- she would read the names of the people who were going to work that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say "she." Was this a lady? And if so, do you know the name of the person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I mean it was not a woman. Those were Dzemal Kapetanovic and Bozo Ninkovic. Those were the persons who issued us work assignments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there some sort of pattern or consistency in the people who issued the work assignment, namely was it the same people or group of people who issued instructions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've mentioned that the instructions were issued to assemble workers from in front of this place called the SDK factory or the communications place. Was the location from which you received your work assignments changed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not as far as I know. That location where we received work assignments applied for a while, and later we were moved to the local commune in the centre of town in order to avoid crowding, because we were 300 or 400 men, so they moved us to the local commune of Serbian Samac and that was our starting point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once that had occurred, was there any change in the procedure that you've described regarding the assembling of the men in the morning, the handing out of assignments, and then the movement of the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Everything was the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: How many workers would be assembled each morning, approximately, and how many trucks would go out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From 300 to 400 workers would assemble and there would be 10 to 15 trucks every morning. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the assembled crowd, were there women?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you become aware of the sorts of work that the women were doing as opposed to men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The women worked on farms around Samac and they went there to milk cows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of hours did you -- over what number of hours did you perform this labour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 10 to 12 hours. We worked from 7.00 to 7.00, depending on the curfew, but on the average, that was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have time off?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Sakib Subasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he participate in this labour that you have described? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see an episode involving him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Describe it, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He asked Bozo Ninkovic for permission to stay at home the next day because it was Bajram, a holiday. Bozo laughed and that Stojan Blagojevic later approached us and said, "Where is the man who wants to celebrate Bajram?" He said, "It's me." And Stojan Blagojevic started beating him in our plain sight. He fell to the ground and Stojan Blogojevic ripped his shirt and saw a tattoo depicting a mosque on his chest. And then Stojan continued kicking him while he was lying down until the guards stopped him. And Sakib was later sent to work as usual in Obudovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did this beating take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was sometime during the last days before my transfer, and it happened outside the SDK building or the building of the communications centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this -- did it occur at a time that the workers were assembling to be given their tasks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you fed when you were performing either the looting or the trench digging?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We got one meal, one can of meat paste a day, of Spam, canned Spam, and sometimes the Serbian troops shared the thick bean soup with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the time that you worked whilst being handed out these assignment, did you ever receive any pay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to make sure that the Chamber understands in summary, therefore, your evidence regarding the looting. Is this the situation: There were numbers of people who were involved in looting. You and the organised workers from the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Private citizens of Serbian background who were free to loot in the villages, and soldiers who were also engaged in the looting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from those categories, was there anyone else involved in looting other than private citizens of Serbian background, soldiers and the groups, the work groups in which you participated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The local Serbian population from the surrounding villages took part in it too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what I mean. They were private citizens just coming in to go shopping, as you put it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to ask you some questions about the two places from which you received your work assignments. One was the SDK communications centre and the other was the community hall or community centre. In the mornings when you were assembled at either of those two locations, did you ever see any of the defendants?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I often saw Mr. Simo Zaric, and when we moved to the local commune, I used to see Miroslav Tadic upstairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What would Mr. Simo Zaric be doing on the occasions that you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He would walk past us on his way to see Bozo and the other people who were making the lists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "us," I want to be absolutely clear. Are you referring to the assembled workers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he walk past the assembled workers when they were assembled both at the SDK factory and the communication -- sorry, and the community centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would he be dressed and what would he be doing, as far as you could tell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a military uniform on. He was armed with a bag, either hanging on his shoulder or carried in his hand. That's how he walked past the soldiers and the assembled workers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as the SDK centre is concerned, do you know where he was going and what he was doing there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what he was doing there but he had to pass by the assembled workers because that was the only entrance that was used also for the communications centre. And just across the road was the entrance that was used by the SDK, so he had no other way to go in. He had to walk past us, the assembled workers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also mentioned Mr. Miroslav Tadic being upstairs at the local commune. Did you see him walk past in the same way as Mr. Zaric or did you see him under different circumstances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him often, since my brother [redacted] worked with him in the local commune, and that's how I saw him. That's why I was able to see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Try and take care not to mention your brother's name. We know which brother you're referring to now but -- that's okay. I know it's difficult but just, if you can remember. Now, you said that your brother worked with him in the local commune and that's how you came to see him. Can you explain that a little more fully to the Chamber? How was it -- or rather, what's the connection between your brother and your seeing Mr. Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know precisely what type of work my brother did, but I think he was a clerk of some sort. He made lists. I don't know what he was doing, but I know that Mr. Tadic was his boss at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And is this brother -- was he a member of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what sort of lists he was making?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you come to see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I often went to see my brother too ask him for a cigarette, and when he saw me, he saw me because the corridor was quite long, and he would tell me, "I told you 100 times not to climb up if you want a cigarette." So I had to go back down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In these times that you're describing, were any of your brothers who were in the 4th Detachment able to assist you or willing to assist you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. My youngest brother left Samac and the two that remained were not willing to help me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went upstairs to try and get a cigarette off your brother, what sort of thing -- what sort of activity could you see that was going on in the community centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw that quite a few people came and when I asked them what they were doing there, they would tell me that they went to get their names signed up for an exchange with Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the ethnic background of the people who you would see trying to get their names signed up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see the men who told the assembled workers downstairs what their work assignments were to be, upstairs in the area around where your brother and Mr. Tadic were located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I did not see these people. They did not say what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, I want to ask you about Odzak. When did you start going to Odzak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After Odzak fell. Odzak fell, I think, on the 7th of July. Sometime around the 10th or perhaps 12th of July, I can't remember the exact date, but it was the first half of July, that's when I started going to Odzak to work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell the Chamber this: Did you get your assignments in Bosanski Samac but that involved going to Odzak to work or did you move to Odzak on a more permanent basis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were assigned to go to Odzak in Samac but in Odzak we were given specific tasks, the things that we had to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know what the military situation was in Odzak prior to Odzak falling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that Odzak was held by the HVO, the Croatian Defence Council, and since I was not there, I did not know what the situation was in Odzak when Odzak fell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the situation in Odzak ever commented on in the -- over the radio, local radio in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the defendants ever comment on the situation in Odzak over the radio?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The town commander, Mr. Simo Zaric, made some comments. He said, on -- over the Serbian radio of Samac, "If Croats do not let the captured Serbs go in Odzak, we will be forced to take reprisals in Samac." And as a result, the camp in the high school was opened and Croats were gathered up and imprisoned there. Whereas the Croat women were imprisoned in the school in Crkvina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's be careful about what was said over the radio and anything that you may have concluded, okay? And let's analyse your last answer a bit more carefully. You said that as a result, the camp in the high school was opened and Croats were gathered up and imprisoned there. And that Croat women were imprisoned in the school in Crkvina. Did those events that you -- that I've just mentioned to you, occur following the radio address by Mr. Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Simo Zaric say that Croats would be gathered up and imprisoned or do you conclude that that is something that occurred in response to the situation in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said that there would be reprisals, and it is my conclusion that the fact that camps appeared in Samac in the high school and the fact that women were taken to the school in Crkvina, that this was the result. That was my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to know why you draw that conclusion. Is it just because of the timing of the speech and those events or do you have any other information that you -- leads you to that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was because of the timing, because when he spoke on the radio, the camp was -- the camps were opened two days later and that is why I connected the two events, the speech and the opening of the camps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall Mr. Simo Zaric ever explaining on radio what precisely the reprisals might be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. He did not explain that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see how the women were rounded up for the Zasavica camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You Saw it with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, tell us all about that, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you want me to go from the beginning, after the -- after the great escape across the Sava River when Muslims swam across into Croatia? The very next day, the military trucks would take the families of all those who managed to escape and take them to Zasavica, the truck went from house to house picking up the women and children according to a list that they had, the list of all the escapees. And the women and children were taken into the trucks with only the clothes that they had on their backs and taken to the camps. I saw when the wife and two children, aged 2 and 4, of Huso Bajraktarevic, I saw them being put onto the truck. And some other cases like that, all over Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about the great escape, as you put it, on another occasion. Let's just concentrate on these trucks and the gathering up of the women and children. Did you see the trucks gathering up the women and children on your way to work or after work? How is it that you had time to see the trucks and this activity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I worked in Samac. I did some work for the town water supply, because the pipes were broke, some of the pipes were broken and that is why I was assigned this work. As I went from street to street shutting down the valves of the town water supply system, I saw women and children being rounded up, gathered up, in Samac. Not only women and children, in fact, but the elderly people too, the grandfathers and grandmothers. They put all those people into trucks, everybody that remained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the ethnic background of these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to get -- I'd like you to paint as clear a picture for the Chamber as you can of what actually was involved. The trucks, first of all, were they open trucks or covered trucks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were covered, but the part of the canvass in the back was pulled up. It was up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were the people being selected and placed on the truck? Was it people off the street? Or was the truck going to homes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Into the houses. The police, the Serbian police, did this, and if somebody was imprisoned, then his family was imprisoned in Zasavica too or if somebody had managed to escape, the same thing would happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The -- tell me this: Did the Serbian police pull up in the truck and go into the house, as far as you could tell? Is that the way it happened? Or were they accompanying the truck in their police cars? How precisely was it carried out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Serbian police officers drove the trucks. One police officer was a driver and he had two police officers as escorts. They had a list and they went from house to house. They knew exactly whom to pick up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the women and children and the elderly people upset?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As you can imagine, they were upset. They had to leave everything behind. They didn't know where they were being taken. They had to leave behind all the things that they had managed to gain in the whole of their lives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many trucks did you see doing this? Was it just the one truck that you saw or was there more than one truck involved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since I only watched this as I passed by, I saw a truck in the Iva Lole Ribara Street where I worked, and that truck was already full of women and children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the men, the Serbian police, who were gathering the men and the women -- sorry, the elderly, the women and the children armed? Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the Serbian police who were doing this locals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most of them were local Serbs from the municipality of Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. At the time that they were being gathered, did you know where they were being taken or is that something that you subsequently learned, that is that they were being taken to Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They didn't know that. I didn't know that. I didn't know where they were being taken. Later, we heard that there was a new camp set up in Zasavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also mentioned that new camps were set up in somewhere else in Bosanski Samac for the Croats. Croat men, I believe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the high school. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And was that set up at about the same time as this episode that you saw with the women being set up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that the camp in Samac was established before the one in Zasavica. The camp in Samac was set up when Mr. Simo Zaric spoke about the reprisals against the local population if they failed to release Serbs from the municipality of Odzak. And there was also the camp in the elementary school in Crkvina and Zasavica is linked with the escape across the Sava River. That was the reprisal that came about after that, because they imprisoned all the family members of those who had escaped, as a sort of reprisal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I think, Witness, now that you've mentioned this escape, it's best if we deal with it now, and the full circumstances under which it occurred and so on. Is there a place in Bosanski Samac called the Spomen Dom

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What exactly is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a memorial to the hero, Mitar Trifunovic, Uco. It was built using the funds provided by the population of Samac to commemorate the work and life and the deeds of this national hero whose name was Mitar Trifunovic, Uco. MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just give me a moment to rearrange my papers? I hadn't anticipated dealing with this topic just at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever attend any meetings there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately when did you go to a meeting there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In June, in late June. An invitation was issued to all the men of military age to report to the Spomen Dom, and I complied. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, you say this, there was an invitation. How was it formulated? How did you find out about it, perhaps, is a better question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It happened for the first time, the notification was issued to us for the first time in front of the local commune where we gathered to go to work. That's where I read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say you read it. I take it that was some written form of -- written form of notification?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What was it, a poster, a signboard, a piece of paper on the ground? Tell us what it was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a poster, A4 size. And it was posted at the entrance to the local commune. In fact, there was a window that belonged to the nursing home, and it was posted there, and the notification was to the effect that all men of military age were to report to the Spomen Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anything on the paper or document that you saw that indicated by whose authority this requirement was being issued?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that there was a seal there, a seal of the Crisis Staff of the Samac municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And was there -- was the poster just on the window of the nursing home or did you see the poster elsewhere around the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also on some other -- elsewhere around the town, so that everybody could see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attend this meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who spoke at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was -- in fact, I'm sure that Jovo Savic addressed the meeting. He was an officer in the army, a reservist. There were also Mladen Radovic, Vlado Sisic and Mr. Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many men attended the meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around 200 people. The hall in the Spomen Dom was full.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What were you informed of at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If we took up guns and became the fighters for the Republika Srpska, we would be relieved of our work duty, and also our families. So whoever took up arms on behalf of Republika Srpska would be relieved of the work duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it made clear to you that whoever took up arms, their families also would be released from work duty? Is that a correct understanding of what you've just said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't think I've asked you what the ethnic background was of the men who attended. Can you please let us know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Simo Zaric speak at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it ever made clear to you what military unit you would be taking up arms with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was only one unit in Samac, and that was the 4th Detachment. So we couldn't belong to any other unit because there weren't any other units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from Mr. Simo Zaric, were there other representatives of the 4th Detachment present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All the people that I enumerated, and Jovo Savic, Mladen Radovic, Vlado Sisic, they were all members of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the men who attended the meeting accept the invitation to join the 4th -- I'm sorry, I'll rephrase my question. Did any of the men who attended the meeting take up arms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very few of them. Perhaps five or six of them, as far as I could see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this meeting, did any significant event take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said a little while ago, there was this great escape across the Sava River, because everybody was afraid of taking up arms, that was the only solution that remained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. di Fazio, I'm interested to know what the period was when this meeting was held, the invitation to take up arms, and what the witness understood taking up arms on behalf of Republika Srpska -- I mean these were residents of Bosanski Samac. What did he understand that to mean? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, I think the witness has already given a time frame in his answer so we've got a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe I missed it. MR. DI FAZIO: We have got a time on that, if you look up in the transcript. I think he's mentioned June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And it's 1.00. Maybe those questions can be asked -- MR. DI FAZIO: I'll clarify those tomorrow, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, 0930 hours. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We will rise and the proceedings will continue tomorrow morning at 0930 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
